agreement_rule.two_or_more_bands_apart: anchor ambiguity - reword, do not average

gates: Neither pole is better. Every dimension runs between two legitimate cultures. “Directed” is not worse than “self-directed.” If you catch yourself scoring toward the pole you personally prefer, stop — that is bias, not signal.

Score the company as it is, not as you would like it. You are describing a culture, not grading it. Aspirational careers-page copy is weak evidence; how people describe daily reality is strong evidence.
Kill the halo. A well-liked brand tends to drag every score toward “good.” Score each dimension only from evidence about that dimension.

Evidence over gut. If you cannot point to a line in the packet that supports the number, lower your confidence. A guess dressed as a 0.9 poisons the ground truth more than an honest 0.5 at low confidence.
Stale culture is wrong culture. Prefer recent evidence. Where the packet flags an evidence-age problem, let it lower your confidence.
Do not search for anything in this packet. If you recognise the company, that is expected and is not a failure — tick the recognition box and keep scoring from the evidence in front of you.

confidence_bands.label: High
confidence_bands.text: Multiple corroborating sources of different types all point the same way.

confidence_bands.label: Medium
confidence_bands.text: Some real evidence but from one source type, or sources partly conflict. A defensible read, not a certain one.

confidence_bands.label: Low
confidence_bands.text: Thin or indirect evidence — a single ambiguous signal. You can defend a direction, but only weakly.

confidence_bands.label: Very low
confidence_bands.text: Almost nothing in the packet bears on this dimension. You are close to guessing.

dimensions.name: Autonomy
dimensions.measures: How much latitude individuals have to set their own approach, priorities and decisions, vs. following assigned direction, defined process and approval chains.
dimensions.where_to_look: Job-post verbs (“execute against the roadmap” vs. “own your domain end-to-end”), number of approval layers, presence of detailed SOP/process docs, review mentions of micromanagement vs. freedom, IC decision rights, remote-trust language.
dimensions.keep_distinct: Not the same as Collaboration. A person can be highly self-directed AND work collectively. Autonomy is about who decides the how; Collaboration is about alone vs. together.

bands.text: Work is assigned and specified top-down. Most decisions need sign-off. Postings stress “follow established processes,” reviews cite micromanagement or rigid procedure.
Manager sets direction and priorities; individual chooses tactics inside clear guardrails. Some latitude, but the frame is given.
Direction set at team level, individuals pick the how within it. No strong signal either way, or genuinely balanced.
ICs own outcomes and choose their approach with light approval. “Ownership,” results-over-process language present.
Individuals set their own priorities and methods with minimal approval. High-trust, flat decision rights pervade the evidence.

dimensions.name: Pace
dimensions.measures: The tempo and intensity of work — deliberate, sustainable cadence vs. rapid, high-urgency, quick-turnaround.
dimensions.where_to_look: “Fast-paced” in postings, release/ship frequency, deadline and crunch culture, review mentions of hours/intensity/burnout vs. calm, on-call expectations.
dimensions.keep_distinct: Not the same as Innovation. A company can move fast while only optimizing, or invent slowly. Pace is tempo; Innovation is novelty.

bands.text: Deliberate cadence, long planning horizons, stability and quality emphasis. Reviews describe a calm, sustainable pace.
Generally measured tempo with occasional pushes. Deadlines exist but rarely dominate.
Ordinary business tempo — some crunch, some calm. No dominant signal.
Regular urgency, frequent releases, tight-ish timelines. Energy is up but not relentless.
“Move fast,” rapid iteration, aggressive deadlines. Reviews cite long hours, intensity or hypergrowth.

dimensions.name: Collaboration
dimensions.measures: How work actually gets produced — individual, heads-down ownership vs. group, cross-functional, in-the-room problem-solving.
dimensions.where_to_look: Team structure (pods/squads vs. individual owners), meeting and pairing culture, open-plan vs. deep-work norms, “we win together” vs. “own your area” language, async-individual vs. sync-group.
dimensions.keep_distinct: Not the same as Autonomy. Collective teams can still hand individuals full ownership of the how. Score meeting and team density here, decision rights under Autonomy.

bands.text: Individual ownership, heads-down norm, low meeting load. Async and individual contribution valued.
Mostly individual work with periodic syncs. Collaboration is coordination, not co-production.
Balanced individual and group work; no dominant mode.
Cross-functional teamwork common, meetings frequent, decisions shared.
Heavy pairing, meeting and consensus culture, cross-functional pods, “we win together” throughout.

dimensions.name: Feedback Culture
dimensions.measures: How performance feedback flows — occasional and softened vs. frequent, direct and unfiltered.
dimensions.where_to_look: “Radical candor” or “direct communication” in values, review-cycle frequency, mentions of blunt vs. supportive delivery, debate and critique norms, conflict-avoidant vs. conflict-embracing signals.
dimensions.keep_distinct: Score the delivery style and frequency of critique, not whether feedback is “nice.” Both poles are legitimate cultures, not good and bad.

bands.text: Feedback is occasional and softened. Harmony valued, conflict avoided, supportive or nurturing framing.
Feedback mostly on cycles, delivered with care. Directness is the exception.
Normal mix of scheduled and ad-hoc feedback, moderate directness.
Frequent, fairly direct feedback; debate is normal; thicker skin helps.
Radical candor, constant unfiltered input, “we tell it straight,” critique and debate are the default.

dimensions.name: Innovation Stance
dimensions.measures: Where the work sits on the create-vs-refine axis — improving and scaling what exists vs. inventing what does not exist yet.
dimensions.where_to_look: R&D emphasis, “0-to-1” vs. “operational excellence” language, product maturity, tolerance for failed bets, “experiment” vs. “scale what works.”
dimensions.keep_distinct: Not the same as Pace. Optimizing can be frantic; inventing can be slow. Score novelty of the work, not its speed.

bands.text: Operational excellence, refine and scale existing product, efficiency focus, mature offering.
Mostly improving known things; occasional new bets at the edges.
Real split between maintaining and creating; no dominant stance.
New-product or new-capability work is common; experimentation encouraged.
R&D-forward, novel products, “0-to-1,” research culture, explicit tolerance for failed experiments.

dimensions.name: Decision Basis
dimensions.measures: What decisions actually rest on — experience, taste and judgement vs. metrics, experiments and analysis.
dimensions.where_to_look: “Data-driven” language, A/B testing and analytics infrastructure, metrics-gated launches, dashboards, vs. founder-gut, design-led or “trust your judgement” signals.
dimensions.keep_distinct: Score the basis of decisions, not their quality. A taste-led company is not worse than a data-led one; they select for different people.

bands.text: Taste, vision and experience lead. Founder gut or design-led; “trust your judgement.”
Judgement-first, data used to confirm rather than decide.
Both judgement and data carry weight depending on the call.
Metrics and experiments usually drive decisions; judgement fills gaps.
“Data-driven,” experiment-gated, metrics-first, A/B-everything, analytics-heavy.
